primitives.note: Wild Cards deals magic damage to enemies hit on a fixed cast-time delay, on cooldown.
Recasting Pick a Card arms Twisted Fate's next basic attack with modified magic damage (Blue/Red/Gold) instead of normal AA damage.
Pick a Card is cast then recast within a 6s cycling window to lock in one of three cards; cooldown starts post-effect (after recast or window timeout).
Pick a Card's recast resets Twisted Fate's basic attack timer.
Mana costs for Q (60-100), W (50-70) and R (100) constrain casts within the 15s window.
Stacked Deck: every 3rd basic attack (stack cap 3) consumes all stacks and deals bonus magic damage; passive attack-speed bonus is a constant untracked flat stat.

needsBespoke.why: Q (plain-cast), W (empowered-attack + recast-or-multipart + attack-reset + resource-budget) and E (nth-hit-or-cast, plus a flat always-on attack-speed stat bonus that needs no dedicated primitive logic) cover the kit's fight-relevant mechanics. R deals no damage and its blink/reveal effects only matter for positioning/vision, which the dummy fight ignores; at most its cast counts as an on-cast trigger, which does not require bespoke logic beyond a plain cast event.

unsettled.question: Which of the three Pick a Card options (Blue/Red/Gold) should the simulated rotation assume is selected on each W recast, given the first hovered card is random and cycling takes 0.5s per card?
options: Always wait for and recast on Blue Card (highest single-target damage + mana restore, up to 1s delay after initial cast)
Recast immediately on whichever card is first hovered (random, averages a lower-damage card some of the time)
Recast on Red Card if AoE/slow is being valued (irrelevant here since there's only one target)
quotes: The first card shown is random but the order always remains the same ({{ai|Blue Card|Twisted Fate}}, {{ai|Red Card|Twisted Fate}}, {{ai|Gold Card|Twisted Fate}}, repeat).
'''Twisted Fate''' cycles through three cards for 6 seconds, hovering each for {{fd|0.5}} seconds at a time.

unsettled.question: Can a single basic attack simultaneously carry both a Pick a Card empowered-attack bonus and an E Stacked Deck 3rd-stack bonus, or are the two on-hit effects mutually exclusive on the same swing?
options: Both effects can stack on the same attack, dealing both bonus amounts
The empowered W attack suppresses/consumes E's on-hit proc trigger for that swing (or vice versa), so only one bonus applies
The two independently proc on whichever attack each is 'ready' on, and in practice they land on different swings
quotes: The empowered attack is special cased to not trigger a stack of {{iis|Fiendhunter Bolts}} {{nie|Opening Barrage}}.
His basic attacks on-hit generate a stack of ''Stacked Deck'', stacking up to 3 times.

unsettled.question: Does Pick a Card's attack-reset (and the empowered attack's own 0.25s cast time) trigger immediately at the moment of recast, or only after the empowered attack's cast time resolves, when computing how many total attacks land in the 15s window?
options: The attack timer resets at the instant of recast, and the 0.25s cast time is additional time before the empowered attack fires
The reset and the empowered attack are effectively simultaneous with normal attack timing, with no extra delay beyond the 0.25s cast
quotes: Pick a Card's recast {{tip|basic attack reset|resets}} '''Twisted Fate's''' basic attack timer.
'''Twisted Fate''' empowers his next  {{tip|basic attack}} within 6 seconds to have a {{fd|0.25}}-second cast time

proposal: Cast R (Destiny) once at the very start purely to register as an ability-activation for any on-cast item effects (it deals no damage and its recast Gate is a repositioning blink with no offensive value against a stationary dummy, so do not recast it).
Cast W (Pick a Card) immediately to begin the card cycle.
Weave in Q (Wild Cards) on cooldown throughout the fight for its magic damage.
Auto-attack continuously between spell casts to build Stacked Deck stacks and deliver its empowered 3rd attack.
Recast W as soon as the Blue Card is hovered (highest damage option) to arm the next basic attack, then keep auto-attacking; repeat W's cast/recast cycle on cooldown.
Continue this loop (Q on cooldown, W cast+Blue-card recast on cooldown, auto-attacks filling the gaps, letting E's 3-stack proc trigger naturally) for the full ~15s fight.
questions: Should R be cast at all in a pure damage-race simulation given it does zero damage itself, or is it better omitted entirely to avoid any mana/time cost?
Does the mana cost of R (100) and Q/W (variable) actually constrain the rotation within 15s at the levels/items being simulated, or is mana effectively unlimited for this kit's short fight?

When W's empowered attack and E's 3-stack proc are both 'ready', which one the engine should resolve into the outgoing basic attack, and whether that choice is deterministic or needs to be modeled as a scheduling assumption?
